definitions.explanation: Having graduated from a prestigious or high-level educational institution, typically a well-known university. In Japanese society, often specifically refers to having attended a top-tier university.

examples.japanese: {高学歴|こうがくれき}の{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い{職場|しょくば}だ。
examples.english: It's a workplace with many highly educated people.

examples.japanese: {高学歴|こうがくれき}だからといって{仕事|しごと}ができるとは{限|かぎ}らない。
examples.english: Having a high educational background doesn't necessarily mean one is good at their job.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{高学歴|こうがくれき}{社会|しゃかい}と{言|い}われることがある。
examples.english: Japan is sometimes called a credential-oriented society.

notes: A compound of {高|こう} (high) + {学歴|がくれき} (educational background/academic credentials). Antonym: {低学歴|ていがくれき} (low educational background). Related terms: {学歴社会|がくれきしゃかい} (credential-oriented society), {学歴|がくれき}フィルター (academic credential filter, informal screening by university prestige in hiring). In Japan, {高学歴|こうがくれき} typically implies graduation from a well-known university rather than simply having an advanced degree.
